questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: If you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to avoid an animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is less dangerous than hitting another car.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When making a turn, look to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Continue using the rear brake.
Swerve the bike toward the side with fewer hazards.
Keep the brake engaged and try to accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, release the brake. However, if the rear brake locks on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is safer.
You are more likely to feel a wind blast from the passing vehicle on the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes it harder to switch gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly while slowly increasing front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay in the right side of your lane.
Move onto the shoulder.
Turn on your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be placed:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere within the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: Which of the following helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Using only the front brake
Using both brakes
Using the center lane
Maintaining or increasing your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Stay out of the center of the lane and follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and gravel that make surfaces slippery.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Not use brakes, but downshift instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, reduce your speed and avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle makes it harder to control the motorcycle.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you NOT use?

options.text: Base trip length on the least experienced rider.
Minimize breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Put inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Minimize breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Base trip length on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce rider fatigue. Put inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may tempt them to move back into your lane too soon. Stay in the center.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the best lane position when traveling through a curve?

options.text: The far left of the lane.
Always the center of the lane.
The far right of the lane.
It changes based on the road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes based on the road curve.
questions.explanation: The best position depends on each curve. The position may even change within a single curve. All curves are different, and road geometry, traffic, and conditions may change as you go through a curve.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press hard on the front brake to prevent the tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes to slow down on slippery surfaces. Gently squeeze the front brake lever and use light pressure on the rear brake to avoid locking the front wheel.

questions.question: When making normal stops, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, even for normal stops. Make this a habit.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, how should you arrange it?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items toward the front of the load. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars take much longer to stop.
Cars take a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles take longer to stop.
They take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes quick stops much harder for motorcycles.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Stop right behind the vehicle quickly.
Stay about four car lengths back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. The vehicle could back up suddenly, or you may need space to escape from a vehicle coming from behind.
